questions.q: Why don't Apex tests make real HTTP callouts?
options: Because callouts always require a Named Credential, which tests can't create
Because Apex tests run outside governor limits and callouts would be unmetered
So tests run reliably and repeatedly without depending on a third-party system being up, fast, or consistent
Because the Http class is unavailable in test context
questions.explain: Real callouts are blocked in test context specifically so tests don't depend on an external system's availability or response, and stay deterministic.

questions.q: Which single method must a class implement to satisfy the HttpCalloutMock interface?
options: execute(HttpRequest req)
mockResponse(String body)
send(HttpRequest req)
respond(HttpRequest req)
questions.explain: HttpCalloutMock requires exactly one method, respond(HttpRequest req), which returns the fake HttpResponse to use.

questions.q: What does Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new MyMock()) do?
options: It registers a mock so that any real callout attempted for the rest of that test method is intercepted and the mock's response is used instead
It creates a new Named Credential for use only in tests
It automatically generates test data for the SObject being queried
It permanently disables all callouts in the org, including in production
questions.explain: Once registered, Test.setMock intercepts callouts during that test method, substituting the mock's respond() return value with no real network call made.

questions.q: If the callout code under test lives inside a managed package, where must Test.setMock be called from?
options: It can be called from any namespace, with no restriction
From a test method in that same package and namespace
Only from an anonymous Apex script, never from a test class
It cannot be used at all for managed package code
questions.explain: For managed package callout code, Test.setMock must be called from a test method in the same package and namespace to successfully intercept the callout.

options: Replacing Named Credentials entirely in production code
Generating a WSDL for a SOAP web service automatically
A built-in mock that reads a fixed response body from a static resource, avoiding the need to hand-write a mock class for simple fixed responses
Publishing a Platform Event during a test
questions.explain: StaticResourceCalloutMock is a built-in alternative to writing a custom HttpCalloutMock class, useful when the fake response is static and doesn't need branching logic.
